newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week-Data unlikely to spark recovery.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week-Data unlikely to spark recovery.

text.p: British government bonds are set to struggle this week, beset by interest rate worries, despite tentative signs of life today, analysts and dealers said Monday.
The market has a raft of domestic data to focus. October retail prices top of the agenda, and the market is likely to be sensitive to unemployment and average earnings figures too.
"With demand continuing to be strong and all led by consumption, along with some worrying price data, it is hard to be too positive on gilts," said Tom Rayner, gilts analyst at Societe Generale.

The Reuters consensus forecast suggests underlying retail prices rose 3.1 percent in October, up from 2.9 percent in September, some way above the government's target of 2.5 percent. The data are due on Thursday.
Analysts said any break above 3.0 percent would be worrying and prompt renewed fears that interest rates will have to rise again soon.
The short sterling strip is discounting another 25 basis point monetary tightening by the year end with March factoring in another half-point rate rise.
"We've seen quite a lot of flattening on the yield curve already and the market is already building in an expectation of further rate increases," said Rayner.
"But any negative surprise on that, the inflation rate or average earnings, could lead to even more flattening."

Don Smith, international economist at HSBC Markets, agreed. "The market is likely to be especially sensitive to data which supports the growing consensus that a further tightening is in the pipeline...and against this backdrop we look for the yield curve to flatten further."
He said the curve between two- and five-years is twice as steep as that between five and 10-years. "There remains plenty of scope for this trend to continue."
The yield spread between two- and five-year gilts was 62 basis points on Monday compared while the five-to-ten-year spread stood at 32 basis points.
On Wednesday, unemployment data for October are due along with average earnings data for September.
The consensus forecast suggests a sharp 25,000 fall in the jobless total after September's massive 35,600 fall.
Underlying average earnings are forecast up 4.0 percent, unchanged from August.

Analysts said given buoyant growth in the UK economy and fears over the size of any tax giveway in the November budget, gilts are unlikely to halt the recent underperformance against key European markets.
The yield spread between gilts and Bunds at 10-years stood at 190 on Monday afternoon compared with 169 basis points before the surprise quarter point rate rise on October 30.
"At such levels gilts look attractive, but this week's data are likely to limit any outperformance," said Dick Howard, senior economist, at Julius Baer Investments.
Rayner said if the data are disappointingly strong, the spread could reach 198 basis points during the week.
"At that level we would probably see more buying as people take advantage of those attractive levels."
Overseas, gilts may enjoy some support from U.S. Treasuries markets which await the October producer and consumer prices and retail sales data.
"This week's data may help the rally continue and a six percent yield at 10-years is possibly," said Howard.
Last week saw the yield on 10-year T-notes hit a new low of 6.24 percent.
Producer prices are due on Wednesday and forecast to show a 0.2 percent monthly rise. On Thursday, consumer prices are forecast to rise 0.3 percent while retail sales are expected up 0.3 percent.
